For the rigid substrate, a 2.5 wt. % SnO2 colloidal dispersion diluted by using deionized water was spincoated on the substrates at 3000 rpm for 30 s and then heated at 150 ° C for 30  min. All ETLs were then treated by UVO for 10  min and transferred to a glovebox.

unresolved_notes: The anti-reflection film is explicitly reported for the champion flexible devices, but its material and deposition details are not supplied; it is therefore retained as a specimen-specific property rather than used to construct an unsupported complete family stack.

The independent certification report identifies sample 1-1# only as a single-junction flexible perovskite solar cell. The evidence does not explicitly establish that it is the same physical device as the reported champion BSP + TSP f-PSC, so it is not linked to that family or champion device.

The stability passages identify devices only as with or without MFCl passivation. Because they do not state whether the MFCl stability specimens used BSP, TSP, or BSP + TSP, the MFCl stability tests are not linked to a specific MFCl family.

The rigid best-performing device occurs in the discussion of the rigid passivation comparison and is represented under the rigid MFCl family, but the exact buried/top placement of MFCl in the rigid finished stack is not stated; its MFCl layer sequence is therefore unresolved.

The main text inconsistently calls the comparison passivator PEAI once. The printed PEACl row in SI Figure S11 explicitly gives Voc = 1.13 V; that value and the figure locator are retained on obs-peacl-comparison-jv. This does not identify it with the separate champion devices.

The I-deficient and Pb-deficient f-PSCs are established as complete photovoltaic devices, but their complete ordered non-absorber stacks are not explicitly restated in the supplied passages. Their family records therefore preserve only the explicitly supported absorber-surface and TSP identities rather than propagating an assumed shared stack.

The source reports TPV decay changing from 0.24 to 1.93 µ s for 'the devices' with MFCl passivation, but it does not identify individual physical devices or report the values as population statistics. No individual-device performance observations were invented for those TPV curves.

The source reports that Pb-deficient f-PSCs exhibit 'a similar trend' after TSP but supplies no atomic numerical outcomes for those populations; no quantitative Pb-deficient population statistic was invented.
Characterization-only perovskite films and hole-only SCLC structures were excluded from photovoltaic device, performance, population, and stability records.

The EQE-integrated JSC of 23.56 mA cm -2 is reported for champion f-PSCs, but the text does not explicitly establish that it was measured on either named champion device; no device-linked observation was added.

The TPV decays from 0.24 to 1.93 µ s are reported for control and MFCl-passivated devices without identifying supported individual devices, so they cannot be added as device-linked performance observations.

The ≈ 60 mV VOC improvement is attributed generally to MFCl passivation at the average-device level, but the passage does not explicitly identify a single passivation family; it was not assigned to pop-flex-double-voc.
